messages:
PagerBot: INCIDENT PAGER — GPU queue length > 95% for pool 'gpu-pool-prod' (alerts: gpu-queue-high, autoscaler-unavailable) :rotating_light:
SRE-Emma: I'm on it, grabbing logs and checking autoscaler status.
Aisha: Seeing sustained queue growth and repeated scale attempts failing with nodegroup errors. Customers hitting rate limits now.
Ben: Linking the autoscaler controller logs: `kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/cluster-autoscaler` shows repeated errors: 
```
E0103 15:02:31.123456 1 scale_up.go:341] failed to find a nodegroup for launchTemplateID: lt-0abcd1234
E0103 15:02:31.123789 1 provider.go:210] launch template mismatch: imageId not found for instance type g4dn.xlarge
```
Connor: The recent launch template change from last night added an extra taint key `gpu:reserved=true` and removed the GPU AMI tag. That would explain no nodes coming up for the GPU ASG.
ML-Oncall: Customers are reporting inference queueing; one internal alert shows 40% increase in latency for hosted API gen endpoints. We should assess degraded customers and notify.
SRE-Emma: Quick mitigation idea: point the ASG used by the autoscaler to a working launch template via `eksctl` and force a scale-up, while we roll back the launch template change. Any objections?
Aisha: +1, do it. Also prepare a temporary node taint removal plan so pods can land on non-reserved GPUs if capacity exists.
Ben: I can patch the launch template in AWS console, but want to avoid race with infra deploys. Suggest we create a temporary NG override and attach to the ASG referenced by autoscaler. Command I'll run: 
```bash
aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name asg-gpu-prod --launch-configuration-name lc-gpu-stable
```
Connor: If we change ASG, autoscaler may reconcile; also need to ensure InstanceProfile/IAM role has ec2:RunInstances for that LT. The logs earlier also showed `ec2:RunInstances denied for role` intermittently.
SRE-Emma: Good catch — check `iam get-role-policy` for the autoscaler node role. Ben, can you also confirm role permissions?
Ben: Checking now. Role `eks-node-role-prod` is missing `ec2:RunInstances` on the new launch template due to a restrictive resource ARN. Will open a quick policy allow for `arn:aws:ec2:::launch-template/lt-0abcd1234` and `ec2:RunInstances` on `*` to be safe.
Deploy-bot: Deploy started: infra/launch-template-revert @ben (CID: d34db33f)
Aisha: While Ben updates IAM, I'm going to remove the `gpu:reserved=true` taint on the node selector used by the daemonset so that pods can land if any GPU nodes show up: 
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch node <node-name> -p '{"spec":{"taints": []}}'
```
ML-Oncall: Customer impact: approx 12% of active API calls are queued beyond 2s; two enterprise customers have reported timeouts. Sending a short status to SRE-Customer-Alerts.
SRE-Emma: Handoff: I'm primary for remediation. @Connor please monitor autoscaler loop and node readiness. @Ben please finish IAM change and revert LT. @Aisha coordinate taint/eviction steps. @ML-Oncall prepare customer-facing note.
Connor: Autoscaler shows attempts to create instance, then fails with `Instance creation failed: LaunchTemplateNotFound` for lt-0abcd1234. After IAM change we should see `RunInstances` succeed.
Ben: IAM policy patched and attached. Reverting launch template to `lt-stable-20260102` and updating ASG now.
Deploy-bot: Revert completed: infra/launch-template-revert (CID: d34db33f) — status: SUCCESS
SRE-Emma: Triggering a manual scale via autoscaler debug: 
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system exec deploy/cluster-autoscaler -- /scale -nodes=4
```
Connor: New EC2 instances launching. Nodes being registered: gpu-node-az1-xx, gpu-node-az2-yy — kubelet registration showing `Ready` for both.
Aisha: Removed taint from one recovered node so best-effort pods can schedule. Evicting pending pods in small batches to avoid a stampede.
ML-Oncall: Latency falling back toward normal. Customer timeouts decreased; enterprise customers notified with ETA ~15m for full recovery.
SRE-Emma: Post-fix check: autoscaler logs now show successful scale up and `scale_up()` returned nodes. No further `launch template mismatch` errors.
Ben: Following up: opened PR to lock launch template deployment to include GPU AMI tag and added a pre-deploy check that validates autoscaler IAM role has permissions.
Connor: Also adding a short-term alert to catch `LaunchTemplateNotFound` spikes and an automation to fallback to a known-good LT ID for critical pools.
ML-Oncall: Customer update sent. No ongoing data loss; only temporary increased latency and some request retries.
SRE-Emma: Incident status: mitigated. Root cause: recent launch template change removed GPU AMI/tag and added restrictive IAM/resource constraints + new taint `gpu:reserved` that prevented pods from scheduling. Action items: 1) revert LT (done), 2) IAM policy hardening + predeploy checks (Ben), 3) taint/label rollout guidance for infra (Aisha), 4) autoscaler fallback automation (Connor), 5) customer postmortem note draft (ML-Oncall).
Aisha: I'll draft the infra guidance and send to infra-owner for sign-off.
Ben: PR link: https://git.company/repo/infra/pull/3499 - includes IAM fix and rollout gating.
Connor: Scheduling postmortem meeting for tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
ML-Oncall: Adding timeline and impact numbers to the postmortem doc.
SRE-Emma: Thanks everyone. Closing pager. :white_check_mark:
PagerBot: Pager resolved: GPU queue returned to normal thresholds.
